```figdown
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 flowchart
title "Change request procedure"

process receive "Receive request"
process validate "Validate"
decision isvalid "Valid?"
process apply "Apply change"
terminator confirm "Confirm success"
terminator rollback "Rollback"

receive -> validate
validate -> isvalid
isvalid -> apply "yes"
apply -> confirm
isvalid -> rollback "no"

group changewindow "change window"
  validate
  apply
```

---

## Commentary

The document declares a flowchart titled "Change request procedure" with the following structure:

**Nodes:**
- Three process boxes: `receive` (incoming requests), `validate` (policy check), and `apply` (implementing changes)
- One decision diamond: `isvalid` (the policy validation outcome)
- Two terminators (endpoints): `confirm` (success path) and `rollback` (failure path)

**Flow:**
The request flows from receive → validate → the decision point. The decision branches: if valid ("yes"), it flows to apply → confirm; if invalid ("no"), it flows directly to rollback.

**Grouping:**
The `group` construct encloses `validate` and `apply` with the label "change window", which draws a bordered box around these two steps so readers immediately see which operations occur within the scheduled maintenance window.

The document uses the experimental `flowchart` genre (v0.1), which includes all the node types and edge-flow syntax needed for this procedure visualization.
